text: You're booking a flight, staring at the seat map. You want a comfortable trip, but your wallet whispers for a good deal.
Ah, the middle seat. It's almost always the cheapest. You click, save a few bucks, ready to endure the squeeze for those savings.
But why is it cheaper? Is it a special discount, or just because nobody really *wants* the middle? You assume it's simply less popular.
Here's the trick: airlines know people value comfort differently. The middle seat is a price-sorting tool, a 'tax' on those who prioritize space.
The cost isn't just discomfort; it reveals exactly how much you're willing to pay for tiny bits of convenience. Airlines extract maximum revenue.
Next time you fly, you'll see the middle seat not as a 'deal,' but a smart, invisible system designed to extract every last dollar.
